chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a muhrim who struck game from which a non-muhrim eats. He said: There is nothing upon the non-muhrim; rather, the fidyah is only upon the muhrim.

key_terms.أَصَابَ: struck or took unlawfully in this legal context
key_terms.الْفِدَاءُ: the expiatory compensation due for violating the ruling
key_terms.الْمُحِلُّ: a person not in the state of ihram
key_terms.صَيْدًا: game animal hunted in the wild
key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: a person in the state of ihram for hajj or 'umrah

ai.seo_question: If a muhrim hunts game and a non-muhrim eats from it, who must pay the fidyah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning game taken by a muhrim during ihram. It states that liability for the expiation belongs only to the muhrim who committed the act, while the non-muhrim who ate from it bears nothing.
